question: Will Russia and Ukraine have a Black Sea maritime ceasefire or safe-passage agreement in effect as of October 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no agreement, with ~11 days until the Oct 29-30 window. Since the grain deal collapsed in July 2023, roughly 5-8 Black Sea truce attempts have produced no mutually confirmed deal that took effect (the March 2025 White House announcement was conditioned by Russia and never took effect). Russia rejected options repeatedly in Sept-Oct 2026 (Lavrov: 'unrealistic'; rejections Oct 3 and Oct 12), the energy truce collapsed Oct 16, and Ukraine demands a combined energy+shipping package. Upside: a new Turkish separate-corridors plan (Oct 19) and a possible US-arranged trilateral technical meeting in late October with the grain corridor on its agenda. No market prices a Black Sea-only deal; Polymarket's general ceasefire markets exclude Black Sea-only agreements, and the Oct 31 general-ceasefire contract was reported at ~7%.

No official reaction from Moscow or Kyiv as of Oct 19.
- ~Sept 25, 2026 (Voice of Emirates / NV): Peskov confirmed Turkey had submitted Black Sea navigation-security proposals (discussed in an Erdogan-Putin meeting) but said no substantive negotiations were underway.

- Sept 28, 2026 (Kyiv Post): Ukraine's agriculture minister Vysotsky said Russia had rejected all grain-truce options and a deal was hard to imagine 'in the coming months'. Question background: Russia rejected a limited Black Sea truce Oct 3 and a 60-day ceasefire Oct 12.
- Oct 1, 2026 (gCaptain/Bloomberg; Pravda.com.ua): Turkey and the UN set up talks with Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue mediators, meetings planned for early October.
- Oct 8, 2026 (Al Jazeera): FM Sybiha said Ukraine would accept an energy + Black Sea shipping ceasefire only as a combined package. A US-proposed trilateral technical meeting (possibly Abu Dhabi) was pushed from early to late October, with the delay blamed on Russia; the grain corridor is on its agenda.
- Mid-Oct 2026: an energy-only truce collapsed by Oct 16 (Ukraine resumed refinery strikes; Zelenskyy said he felt 'betrayed' by Trump).
- Precedent, March 2025: the White House announced a Black Sea agreement; Russia conditioned it on sanctions relief and it never took effect.
- Base rate: Black Sea truce attempts since July 2023 (roughly 5-8 distinct initiatives): 0 produced a mutually confirmed agreement that took effect.
- Markets: no Black Sea-only market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi; Polymarket general ceasefire markets exclude Black Sea-only deals.
- Status quo: no bilateral shipping/port agreement in effect.
- Resolves off public confirmation by official representatives of both Russia and Ukraine of a mutually agreed shipping/port attack halt (a general ceasefire counts), not off proposals or unilateral statements.
- Event window: Oct 29 00:00 UTC -> Oct 30 23:59 UTC 2026 (a deal announced earlier counts if still in effect then); as of Oct 19 the window has not started (~0% elapsed), and ~9.25 days remain until it opens.
- Searched but not found: any Russian or Ukrainian official response to the Oct 19 Turkish plan; a confirmed date for the late-October trilateral meeting.
